<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915617_theRebbe_822" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915617_theRebbe_822__p008">
  <section v="21">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>There are two types of miracles that are above nature, and even those not clothed in nature can be mistaken for nature, as with the manna for forty years, unlike the miracle of the Splitting of the Sea.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And to add,</t>
    <t s="1">that even in miracles that are above nature,</t>
    <t s="2">there are two types.</t>
    <t s="3">For although the miracles are not clothed in nature,</t>
    <t s="4">nevertheless, there is room for error that they are nature.</t>
    <t s="5">And like the descent of the manna during forty years,</t>
    <t s="6">for although the miracle was not clothed in nature</t>
    <t s="7">[and as the Rambam wrote,</t>
    <t s="8">that the sojourn of Israel in the desert for forty years and the existence of the manna there is among the greatest wonders,</t>
    <t s="9">for the nature of the desert is not a place of seed, etc.,</t>
    <t s="10">and it is impossible for there to be bread in it</t>
    <t s="11">(neither bread from the earth nor bread from the heavens).</t>
    <t s="12">And all the more so that it had no waste,</t>
    <t s="13">and even more so that the one who gathered little did not lack,</t>
    <t s="14">for from the perspective of the nature of the world there is no place for this],</t>
    <t s="15">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="16">because the miracle was for forty years there was room for error that it is nature.</t>
    <t s="17">And that the miracle is in such revelation that there is no giving of place at all for error that it is nature,</t>
    <t s="18">like the miracle of the Splitting of the Sea.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="22">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The root of miracles above nature is from the name Havayah, while the root of miracles clothed in nature is from the name Sha-dai, with two explanations regarding their source.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">And he continues in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="2">that regarding the distinction between the two types</t>
    <t s="3">(miracles above nature and miracles clothed in nature)</t>
    <t s="4">in their root,</t>
    <t s="5">there are two explanations.</t>
    <t s="6">For the root of miracles above nature is from the name Havayah,</t>
    <t s="7">and the root of miracles clothed in nature is from the name Sha-dai,</t>
    <t s="8">"Sha-dai" [means] that My Elokus is sufficient for every creature.</t>
    <t s="9">[And the distinction of the two modes in the miracles clothed in nature themselves is,</t>
    <t s="10">that the name Sha-dai is in Yesod,</t>
    <t s="11">that its drawing down below is through Malchus.</t>
    <t s="12">And in this there are two modes.</t>
    <t s="13">Their drawing down through Malchus is in the manner of passing through or in the manner of clothing.</t>
    <t s="14">And they are the root of the two modes in miracles].</t>
    <t s="15">For according to this explanation,</t>
    <t s="16">the distinction between the two types of miracles is</t>
    <t s="17">(also)</t>
    <t s="18">in their root.</t>
    <t s="19">And another explanation,</t>
    <t s="20">that the miracles clothed in nature are from the aspect of "I" as it is clothed in the nothingness of Malchus.</t>
    <t s="21">(And it is in the manner explained elsewhere</t>
    <t s="22">that the root of miracles clothed in nature is from the name Havayah as it is clothed in the name Adnus).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="23">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Based on the earlier explanation, the four types of miracles correspond to the four letters of the name Havayah, with the letters yud and hei being above nature and vav and hei being clothed in nature.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And according to what was explained above</t>
    <t s="1">(in section 8)</t>
    <t s="2">that the multiplicity of types of miracles is in that which is above the chain of descent</t>
    <t s="3">(for in order for them to be drawn down into the chain of descent there is multiplicity above the chain of descent)</t>
    <t s="4">it can be said,</t>
    <t s="5">that the four types of miracles have their root in the four letters of the name Havayah.</t>
    <t s="6">For the miracles drawn from the letters vav and hei, which are related to the worlds</t>
    <t s="7">(vav and hei are revealed),</t>
    <t s="8">are clothed in nature.</t>
    <t s="9">And as in the letters vav and hei,</t>
    <t s="10">the vav is a single line drawn from above to below, meaning that even when drawn below it is connected with above,</t>
    <t s="11">and the hei is in the form of length and width</t>
    <t s="12">(in which only the receiving surface is noticeable),</t>
    <t s="13">so too is it regarding the miracles drawn from the letters vav and hei,</t>
    <t s="14">that the miracles drawn from the vav, even after they are drawn and clothed in the garments of nature, are noticeably revealed as miracles,</t>
    <t s="15">and the miracles drawn from the final hei, after they are drawn and clothed in the garments of nature, only the nature in which the miracles are clothed is revealed</t>
    <t s="16">(the receiving surface).</t>
    <t s="17">And the miracles drawn from the letters yud and hei, which are above relation to the worlds</t>
    <t s="18">(yud and hei are hidden),</t>
    <t s="19">are above being clothed in nature,</t>
    <t s="20">and within themselves there are two types.</t>
    <t s="21">For the letter hei, which has the form of length and width,</t>
    <t s="22">through which it is possible for there to be grasp in it—therefore,</t>
    <t s="23">in the level of miracles drawn from it there is a giving of place to nature.</t>
    <t s="24">For although the miracles themselves are not clothed in nature, nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="25">relative to this level,</t>
    <t s="26">nature is not negated,</t>
    <t s="27">and therefore there is room for error that they are nature.</t>
    <t s="28">And relative to the level of miracles drawn from the letter yud, which is only a point that has no grasp in it,</t>
    <t s="29">there is no place for nature,</t>
    <t s="30">and therefore in these miracles it is not possible to err that they are nature.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
